content.text:
I've reviewed all sections of the agreement, including the definitions (Field of Use), Article II license grant/restrictions, the fee and supplemental payment provisions, Article XXII (Right of First Refusal), and the general provisions.

Findings:
- The license is expressly **non-exclusive** (p0001, p0030, p0043, p0049) — no sole-supplier or exclusive-dealing covenant is imposed on the Licensee.
- The "Right of First Refusal" (p0139) flagged by the planner is a **change-of-control/asset-sale** first refusal, not a sourcing or first-call exclusivity, so it falls outside this rule (it is a restrictive M&A right, addressed by other rules).
- "FIELD OF USE" (p0007) uses "exclusive purpose" only to narrow how we may use Licensor's technology; it does not restrict us from procuring competing FX platforms or services from third parties.
- Article II(ii) (p0027) and Article VI (p0085) restrict onward distribution of Licensor's technology — standard IP scope limits, not exclusive dealing.
- No "sole and exclusive provider", "all of its requirements", or "shall not procure from any third party" language exists anywhere in the document.

No exclusivity obligation binds us, so the preferred position is already met and no redline is warranted.

input.quote: grants to Licensee a non-exclusive license to utilize Licensed Technology solely in the Field of Use and subject to the additional restrictions set forth below and otherwise in this License Agreement.
input.rationale: The Agreement imposes no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation on us. The grant is expressly non-exclusive (p0001, p0030, p0043, p0049), and nothing requires us to source our FX platform, liquidity or related services solely from Licensor or bars us from procuring from third parties. The "FIELD OF USE" definition (p0007) uses "exclusive purpose" only to limit the permitted use of Licensor's technology, and Article II(ii) (p0027) and Article VI (p0085) are onward-distribution/IP scope limits — neither restricts our freedom to buy elsewhere. The "Right of First Refusal" in Article XXII (p0139) is triggered only by a third-party offer to buy our assets or a merger/consolidation, i.e. a change-of-control first refusal, not a first-call or exclusive-dealing right over our purchasing. Accordingly the preferred position (no exclusivity binding Customer) is already satisfied and no redline is required for this rule.
